Marta: FYI - after the driver rollout to fleet-3 (525.85 -> 531.41) last night we're seeing MIG profiles disappear on a subset of A100 nodes in us-west1.

aj: which hosts and any common kernel/instance details?

Marta: affected node IDs: gpu-w3-12, gpu-w3-15, gpu-w3-18. All are A100-40GB, kernel 5.15.0-101. Kubelet logs show pods can't find expected /dev/mig devices.

sanjay: can you paste nvidia-smi from an affected host? quick checks: driver version, uuid, mig list.

Marta: output from gpu-w3-12 below:
```
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-1111-2222-3333)
$ nvidia-smi mig -lgi
No MIG devices found.
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_name,gpu_uuid,driver_version --format=csv
NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, GPU-1111-2222-3333, 531.41
```

aj: driver bumped but no MIG partitions. Any errors in dkms or dmesg during module load?

Marta: dkms reported success, but dmesg shows this after reboot:
```
NVRM: GPU UUID mismatch: expected GPU-aaaa-bbbb but found GPU-1111-2222-3333
mig: failed to load device profiles: profile table invalid
```

infra-bot: Deploy job #deploy/driver-rollout-2026-03 completed on 2026-03-17T23:48:52Z (success 92% of targets; 8 failures flagged).

kevin: "UUID mismatch" sounds like the regression we encountered in driver 531.x where internal device indexing changed and our MIG rehydrate logic assumes stable UUIDs. If the kernel module was built against a different kernel patch level it can wipe MIG metadata.

sanjay: confirmed: there's a known bug in 531.41 + kernel 5.15 that can clear MIG profile tables when module is recreated. Also flag: our NCCL build (2.15) expects a certain NVLink enumeration on these SKUs which could complicate in-place fixes.

aj: options ordered by blast radius:
1) Roll back the driver to 525.85 on failed nodes (fastest path to restore MIG).
2) Attempt in-place MIG reconfiguration with a script that remaps UUIDs (risky: will disrupt pods and may still fail).
3) Reboot nodes into a validated kernel (5.19) where 531.41 behaved correctly (longer lead time).

Marta: rollback seems safest for prod. In-place reconfigure might not work because of the UUID mismatch error.

ops-oncall: I can run a targeted rollback for the failed hosts and patch the rollout job to exclude fleet-3 until we have a fix. ETA ~30m for first batch.

kevin: make sure to capture pre/post nvidia-smi and run `nvidia-smi -q -d MIG` to see any residual fragments. If rollback doesn't restore MIG profiles we may need to reprovision with `nvidia-smi mig -C` which will generate new MIG UUIDs and force node re-registration.

sanjay: dev/infra action: I'll update our mig-rehydrate script to detect UUID drift, write backups to /var/lib/redwood/mig-uuid-backup, and provide a --force-mapping fallback. I'll open a PR now.

Marta: please proceed with rollback on gpu-w3-12 and gpu-w3-15. Keep gpu-w3-18 as canary for attempting the in-place recovery path.

aj: starting rollback on gpu-w3-12: 
```
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-525=525.85-1 && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo reboot
```

infra-bot: @aj started rollback on gpu-w3-12 (job 8342). Progress: 1/2 nodes in batch complete.

aj: gpu-w3-12 back online. nvidia-smi now: 
```
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-1111-2222-3333)
$ nvidia-smi mig -lgi
GPU 0: MIG device 0: 1g.5gb (ID: MIG-GPU-1111-2222-3333-0)
```

Marta: good sign. Proceed with gpu-w3-15 next.

ops-oncall: updating the rollout job to pin driver 525.85 for fleet-3 and adding a post-install preflight that runs `nvidia-smi mig -lgi`. Also adding a failure flag to halt further batches.

kevin: follow-ups:
- Rollback remaining failure nodes (ops-oncall)
- Add UUID backup and force-mapping to rehydrate script (sanjay)
- Reproduce in staging (kernel 5.15 + driver 531.41) and file with NVIDIA if repro'd (kevin)

sanjay: opened PR for script changes and added unit tests to simulate UUID drift.

Marta: thanks. I'll monitor MIG-backed pods for 1h and then close incident if stable. Added a runbook note to pause driver rollouts when kernels differ or when MIG devices are detected on hosts. :memo:

infra-bot: Incident marked high-priority. Assigned to ops-oncall, kevin, sanjay.
